newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia shutting down agricultural office.
newsitem.headline: Colombia shutting down agricultural office.

text.p: Colombia decided to shut the state-run agency that once controlled all of its agricultural imports and fixed support prices for crops at home, government officials said Wednesday.

Agriculture Minister Ceclia Lopez said the National Agricultural Marketing Institute, IDEMA, would be closed by March of next year and replaced by a smaller government office that will promote the sale of Colombian agricultural products aboard.
According to Lopez, IDEMA registered heavy losses last year totalling nearly $100 million.

Most of its functions, including tenders for rice, wheat and other agricultural imports, had been taken over by the private sector in the aftermath of Colombia's economic opening in the early 1990s, she said.
Most of its 1,300 employees would be offered voluntary retirement and severance pay, she said, adding that only some would be offered work in the new government agency.
